chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no ablution (wudu) required for kissing, nor for touching the private parts, nor for sexual contact.
ai.seo_question: Does kissing or touching the private parts break wudu in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between minor and major impurity by ruling that kissing, touching the private parts, and general sexual contact (mubasharah) do not break wudu, reserving the nullification of ablution primarily for the emergence of excretions or deep sleep. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between acts that require ghusl (full ritual bath) and those that only require wudu, emphasizing that physical intimacy alone does not invalidate the state of minor purity unless accompanied by specific conditions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is neither an Ablution (Wudhu) for the kissing, nor from touching the private parts, nor the contact (hugging etc.)’.
en.sarwar: 12. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not necessary to take Wudu’ for kissing, touching private parts or because of contact.’”
